title: Activate public distribution: tap repo, TAP_TOKEN, first release
description:
Everything is built and CI-verified; these are the outward-facing steps left, all requiring account-level actions.

1. gh repo edit panchr/espresso --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences
2. gh repo create panchr/homebrew-tap --public --add-readme --description 'Homebrew tap for panchr'
3. Fine-grained PAT scoped to homebrew-tap with Contents: read+write, then: gh secret set TAP_TOKEN
4. git tag v0.1 && git push origin v0.1

Step 4 publishes the release and pushes the stamped cask. Without step 3 the release still succeeds and the tap step is skipped with a notice. First release is v0.1 (pre-1.0); verified the two-component tag stamps the bundle and orders correctly in Homebrew.
design: Cask installs prebuilt artifacts only, so GitHub releases stay the distribution unit; the cask is a checksum-stamped pointer at them.
close_reason: Repo public, v0.1 released, tap created and cask published; only the CI automation token remains

title: Prepare repo for public release + one-line installer
description: Make the repo publishable: license, CI, tagged release workflow that builds a universal Espresso.app, and a curl-able install.sh so users can install without a Swift toolchain.
close_reason: Release plumbing, installer, and docs landed; repo stays private for now

title: Add TAP_TOKEN so releases auto-update the Homebrew cask
description:
The v0.1 cask was pushed to panchr/homebrew-tap by hand. Until TAP_TOKEN exists, every future release needs that manual push.

Setup: create a fine-grained PAT scoped to panchr/homebrew-tap with Contents: read+write, then in the espresso repo run: gh secret set TAP_TOKEN

The release workflow picks it up automatically on the next tag. To publish the cask for an already-tagged release: gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=vX.Y
